Kalman filtering and state estimation

Track a hidden state through noisy measurements. Every Bayesian step is a Gaussian collapse; every prediction is an ellipse puffing up.

blocks.html:
1. The estimation problem

You can't see the thing you care about. A satellite's true position, a circuit's hidden voltage, a stock's latent volatility — the state $x_t$ is hidden behind a noisy sensor reading $y_t$, and the sensor lies. The state itself moves under its own dynamics, which you only know up to a noise term. Estimation is the art of fusing what physics predicts with what the sensor saw, and keeping a calibrated sense of your own uncertainty as you go.

The linear-Gaussian setting writes both pieces as $$x_{t+1} = F\,x_t + w_t,\qquad y_t = H\,x_t + v_t,$$ with mutually independent zero-mean Gaussian noises $w_t\sim\mathcal{N}(0,Q)$ and $v_t\sim\mathcal{N}(0,R)$. The matrix $F$ encodes the dynamics ("if I'm at $x$ now, where will I be next?"), $H$ encodes which projection of the state the sensor sees, and $Q$, $R$ encode how much you trust each side.

The miracle that makes Kalman work: if you start with a Gaussian prior over $x_0$, then every $p(x_t\mid y_{1:t})$ stays Gaussian forever. Two numbers per dimension — a mean and a covariance — describe your belief exactly, with no moment approximation.

<script>
(function(){
  const svg = document.getElementById('setup-svg');
  const Rs = document.getElementById('setup-R');
  const Rv = document.getElementById('setup-Rv');
  const out = document.getElementById('setup-out');
  const N = 60, W=760, H=240, pad=30;
  // deterministic "truth": sin + drift
  const truth = Array.from({length:N}, (_,i)=>{
    const t = i/(N-1);
    return 1.2*Math.sin(2*Math.PI*1.3*t) + 0.6*t - 0.2;
  });
  // deterministic Gaussian noise samples (Box-Muller from a fixed seed)
  let seed = 7919;
  function rand(){ seed = (seed*1664525+1013904223)>>>0; return seed/4294967296; }
  const u1 = Array.from({length:N}, rand);
  const u2 = Array.from({length:N}, rand);
  const z = u1.map((u,i)=> Math.sqrt(-2*Math.log(u+1e-9))*Math.cos(2*Math.PI*u2[i]));
  function draw(){
    while(svg.firstChild) svg.removeChild(svg.firstChild);
    const R = parseFloat(Rs.value);
    Rv.textContent = 'R = '+R.toFixed(2);
    const ymin=-2.2, ymax=2.2;
    const X = i => pad + (W-2*pad)*i/(N-1);
    const Y = v => H-pad - (H-2*pad)*(v-ymin)/(ymax-ymin);
    // axes
    svg.appendChild(SVG('line',{x1:pad,y1:Y(0),x2:W-pad,y2:Y(0),stroke:'var(--line)','stroke-dasharray':'3 3'}));
    // truth line
    let d = '';
    for(let i=0;i<N;i++){ d += (i?'L':'M')+X(i)+' '+Y(truth[i]); }
    svg.appendChild(SVG('path',{d,fill:'none',stroke:'var(--cyan)','stroke-width':2}));
    // observations
    const sd = Math.sqrt(R);
    let sse = 0;
    for(let i=0;i<N;i++){
      const obs = truth[i] + sd*z[i];
      sse += (obs-truth[i])*(obs-truth[i]);
      svg.appendChild(SVG('circle',{cx:X(i),cy:Y(obs),r:2.6,fill:'var(--yellow)','fill-opacity':0.85}));
    }
    // legend
    const lg = SVG('g',{transform:'translate('+(W-180)+',18)'});
    lg.appendChild(SVG('line',{x1:0,y1:8,x2:24,y2:8,stroke:'var(--cyan)','stroke-width':2}));
    const t1 = SVG('text',{x:30,y:12,'font-size':12,fill:'var(--mute)'}); t1.textContent='true state xₜ'; lg.appendChild(t1);

2. Bayesian fusion of two Gaussians

Before tackling time, do the static problem: two independent witnesses report scalar Gaussian beliefs about the same quantity. Witness 1 says $\mathcal{N}(\mu_1,\sigma_1^2)$; witness 2 says $\mathcal{N}(\mu_2,\sigma_2^2)$. Bayes multiplies the two densities and renormalises. Both exponents are quadratic in $x$, so the log-posterior is

$$-\tfrac12\!\left[\frac{(x-\mu_1)^2}{\sigma_1^2}+\frac{(x-\mu_2)^2}{\sigma_2^2}\right] = -\tfrac12\!\left[\!\left(\tfrac{1}{\sigma_1^2}+\tfrac{1}{\sigma_2^2}\right)\!x^2 - 2\!\left(\tfrac{\mu_1}{\sigma_1^2}+\tfrac{\mu_2}{\sigma_2^2}\right)\!x\right] + \text{const}.$$

The coefficient of $x^2$ is the posterior precision (inverse variance); the coefficient of $-2x$ divided by twice the precision is the posterior mean. Read them off:

$$\frac{1}{\sigma^2} = \frac{1}{\sigma_1^2}+\frac{1}{\sigma_2^2},\qquad \mu = \sigma^2\left(\frac{\mu_1}{\sigma_1^2}+\frac{\mu_2}{\sigma_2^2}\right).$$

Precisions add. The combined width is sharper than either input — even a hazy second witness narrows the picture. The combined mean is the precision-weighted average of $\mu_1,\mu_2$: the witness you trust more pulls the answer toward itself.

  function path(m,s,scale){
    let d=''; const xs = 240;
    for(let i=0;i<=xs;i++){
      const x = xmin + (xmax-xmin)*i/xs;
      const y = bell(x,m,s)*scale;

3. The 1D Kalman cycle — predict and update

Step the scalar state $x_{t+1}=a\,x_t+w_t$ forward, then observe $y_t = x_t + v_t$. Run the belief $\mathcal{N}(\hat x_t,\sigma_t^2)$ through two micro-moves:

StepMeanVariance
predict (no data)$\hat x_{t+1\mid t} = a\,\hat x_{t\mid t}$$\sigma_{t+1\mid t}^2 = a^2\sigma_{t\mid t}^2 + q$
update (with $y_{t+1}$)$\hat x_{t+1\mid t+1} = \hat x_{t+1\mid t} + K_{t+1}(y_{t+1}-\hat x_{t+1\mid t})$$\sigma_{t+1\mid t+1}^2 = (1-K_{t+1})\sigma_{t+1\mid t}^2$

The scalar gain is $K_{t+1} = \sigma_{t+1\mid t}^2/(\sigma_{t+1\mid t}^2 + r)$ — exactly the fusion formula in disguise, applied to "my prediction" and "the new observation." A noisy observation ($r$ large) sends $K\to0$ and the filter ignores $y$; a clean observation ($r$ small) sends $K\to1$ and the filter accepts $y$ wholesale.

Iterating predict + update settles the variance into a fixed point $\sigma_*^2$ that solves $\sigma_*^2 = (1-K_*)(a^2\sigma_*^2 + q)$ — the scalar steady-state Riccati equation (a generic name for the quadratic-in-$\sigma^2$ recurrences that govern covariance evolution in linear-Gaussian estimation and control). After that the filter runs in a regime where the predict-inflation and update-shrinkage exactly cancel.

The widget below specialises to $a=1$ (pure random walk) so the recurrence is easy to read; for $|a|<1$ the steady-state $\sigma_*^2$ would be even smaller (mean-reverting dynamics damp predict-inflation), and for $|a|>1$ the variance can blow up faster than the filter can shrink it. The qualitative pattern of breathe-and-settle is the same.

    return () => {
      s = (s*1664525+1013904223)>>>0;
      const u1 = s/4294967296;
      s = (s*1664525+1013904223)>>>0;
      const u2 = s/4294967296;
      return Math.sqrt(-2*Math.log(u1+1e-9))*Math.cos(2*Math.PI*u2);
    };
  }
  function reset(){
    state = {
      t: 0,
      phase: 'predict', // next move to take
      xhat: 0,
      sig2: 1.0,
      truth: [0.5],
      obs: [],
      means: [0],
      vars: [1.0],
      qRand: makeStream(11003),
      rRand: makeStream(23071)
    };
    draw();
  }
  function step(){
    const q = parseFloat(qSl.value);
    const r = parseFloat(rSl.value);
    if(state.phase === 'predict'){
      // truth steps
      const tnext = a*state.truth[state.truth.length-1] + Math.sqrt(q)*state.qRand();
      state.truth.push(tnext);
      // predict
      state.xhat = a*state.xhat;
      state.sig2 = a*a*state.sig2 + q;
      state.means.push(state.xhat);
      state.vars.push(state.sig2);
      state.phase = 'update';
    } else {
      // observe
      const y = state.truth[state.truth.length-1] + Math.sqrt(r)*state.rRand();
      state.obs.push(y);
      const K = state.sig2 / (state.sig2 + r);
      state.xhat = state.xhat + K*(y - state.xhat);
      state.sig2 = (1-K)*state.sig2;
      state.means[state.means.length-1] = state.xhat;
      state.vars[state.vars.length-1] = state.sig2;
      state.t += 1;
      state.phase = 'predict';
    }
    if(state.truth.length > Nmax){
      state.truth.shift(); state.means.shift(); state.vars.shift();
      if(state.obs.length) state.obs.shift();
    }
    draw();
  }
  function draw(){
    while(svg.firstChild) svg.removeChild(svg.firstChild);
    const ymin=-3.5, ymax=3.5;
    const n = state.truth.length;
    const X = i => pad + (W-2*pad)*i/Math.max(1,Nmax-1);
    const Y = v => Hh-pad - (Hh-2*pad)*(v-ymin)/(ymax-ymin);
    svg.appendChild(SVG('line',{x1:pad,y1:Y(0),x2:W-pad,y2:Y(0),stroke:'var(--line)','stroke-dasharray':'3 3'}));
    // shaded ±2σ band around filter mean
    let dUpper='', dLower='';
    for(let i=0;i<n;i++){
      const sd = Math.sqrt(state.vars[i]);
      dUpper += (i?'L':'M')+X(i)+' '+Y(state.means[i]+2*sd);
      dLower += 'L'+X(i)+' '+Y(state.means[i]-2*sd);
    }
    if(n>1){
      // reverse the lower path for closing
      let dRev='';
      for(let i=n-1;i>=0;i--){
        const sd = Math.sqrt(state.vars[i]);
        dRev += (i===n-1?'L':'L')+X(i)+' '+Y(state.means[i]-2*sd);
      }
      svg.appendChild(SVG('path',{d:dUpper+dRev+'Z',fill:'var(--yellow)','fill-opacity':0.13,stroke:'none'}));
    }
    // truth
    let dT=''; for(let i=0;i<n;i++) dT+=(i?'L':'M')+X(i)+' '+Y(state.truth[i]);
    svg.appendChild(SVG('path',{d:dT,fill:'none',stroke:'var(--cyan)','stroke-width':2}));
    // means
    let dM=''; for(let i=0;i<n;i++) dM+=(i?'L':'M')+X(i)+' '+Y(state.means[i]);
    svg.appendChild(SVG('path',{d:dM,fill:'none',stroke:'var(--yellow)','stroke-width':2}));
    // obs dots
    for(let i=0;i<state.obs.length;i++){
      svg.appendChild(SVG('circle',{cx:X(i+1),cy:Y(state.obs[i]),r:3,fill:'var(--pink)'}));
    }
    // legend
    const lg = SVG('g',{transform:'translate('+(W-200)+',16)'});
    [['var(--cyan)','truth',true], ['var(--yellow)','filter mean',true], ['var(--pink)','obs',false]].forEach(([c,n2,line],i)=>{
      if(line){
        lg.appendChild(SVG('line',{x1:0,y1:8+i*16,x2:18,y2:8+i*16,stroke:c,'stroke-width':2}));
      } else {
        lg.appendChild(SVG('circle',{cx:9,cy:8+i*16,r:3,fill:c}));
      }
      const t = SVG('text',{x:24,y:12+i*16,'font-size':12,fill:'var(--mute)'}); t.textContent=n2; lg.appendChild(t);
    });
    svg.appendChild(lg);
    const sd = Math.sqrt(state.vars[state.vars.length-1]);
    const r = parseFloat(rSl.value);
    const sig2pred = state.vars[state.vars.length-1]; // after current move
    const K = sig2pred/(sig2pred + r);
    out.textContent = 'next move: '+state.phase+'    t='+state.t+'    σ = '+sd.toFixed(3)+
      (state.phase==='update'? '    next K ≈ '+K.toFixed(3) : '');
  }
  stepBtn.addEventListener('click', step);
  resetBtn.addEventListener('click', reset);
  [qSl,rSl].forEach(el=> el.addEventListener('input', draw));
  reset();
})();
</script>

4. Vector form and the covariance ellipse

Lift everything to $\mathbb{R}^n$. The scalar variance $\sigma^2$ becomes a covariance matrix $\Sigma$ — same role, just symmetric and positive-definite instead of scalar (implementations often call this matrix $P$; both symbols mean the same thing, and the §6 widget exposes $P$ in its readout to match the convention used in tracking code).

The mean $\hat x$ is a vector; the covariance $\Sigma$ is a positive-definite matrix you can picture as an ellipse $\{x : (x-\hat x)^\top\Sigma^{-1}(x-\hat x) = 1\}$. The principal axes of that ellipse are the eigenvectors of $\Sigma$, and their lengths are the square roots of the eigenvalues.

The two moves become matrix moves:

$$\Sigma_{t+1\mid t} = F\,\Sigma_{t\mid t}\,F^\top + Q,\qquad \Sigma_{t+1\mid t+1} = (I - K_{t+1}H)\,\Sigma_{t+1\mid t}.$$

Read the prediction step geometrically: $F$ rotates and stretches the ellipse (the deterministic part of "where will I be next?"); then $+Q$ puffs it up isotropically (or anisotropically — $Q$ has its own shape). The update step is the dual move. The observation matrix $H$ picks out a subspace; the gain $K$ collapses the ellipse along that subspace by as much as the observation's precision allows.

<script>
(function(){
  const svg = document.getElementById('ell-svg');
  const out = document.getElementById('ell-out');
  const modeX = document.getElementById('ell-mode-x');
  const modeY = document.getElementById('ell-mode-y');
  const stepBtn = document.getElementById('ell-step');
  const resetBtn = document.getElementById('ell-reset');
  // 2x2 matrix helpers
  function matmul(A,B){
    return [[A[0][0]*B[0][0]+A[0][1]*B[1][0], A[0][0]*B[0][1]+A[0][1]*B[1][1]],
            [A[1][0]*B[0][0]+A[1][1]*B[1][0], A[1][0]*B[0][1]+A[1][1]*B[1][1]]];
  }
  function mattrans(A){ return [[A[0][0],A[1][0]],[A[0][1],A[1][1]]]; }
  function matadd(A,B){ return [[A[0][0]+B[0][0],A[0][1]+B[0][1]],[A[1][0]+B[1][0],A[1][1]+B[1][1]]]; }
  function eig2(A){
    // returns {l1,l2,v1,v2} for symmetric 2x2
    const a=A[0][0], b=A[0][1], d=A[1][1];
    const tr = a+d, det = a*d - b*b;
    const disc = Math.max(0, tr*tr/4 - det);
    const l1 = tr/2 + Math.sqrt(disc), l2 = tr/2 - Math.sqrt(disc);
    let v1;
    if(Math.abs(b) > 1e-9) v1 = [b, l1-a];
    else v1 = (a >= d) ? [1,0] : [0,1];
    const n = Math.hypot(v1[0],v1[1])||1; v1=[v1[0]/n, v1[1]/n];
    const v2 = [-v1[1], v1[0]];
    return {l1:Math.max(1e-9,l1), l2:Math.max(1e-9,l2), v1, v2};
  }
  // initial belief: F = small rotation+stretch, Q small, R given by mode
  const F = [[1.0, 0.3],[0.0, 1.0]];        // shear
  const Q = [[0.06, 0.0],[0.0, 0.06]];
  const r = 0.15;
  let state;
  function reset(){
    state = {
      Sigma: [[0.6, 0.4],[0.4, 0.9]],
      history: [],
      phase: 'predict',
      mode: 'x'
    };
    draw();
  }
  function step(){
    if(state.phase === 'predict'){
      state.history.push({label:'before predict', S: state.Sigma});
      state.Sigma = matadd(matmul(matmul(F, state.Sigma), mattrans(F)), Q);
      state.phase = 'update';
    } else {
      state.history.push({label:'after predict', S: state.Sigma});
      // H is [1,0] or [0,1]
      const H = state.mode==='x' ? [1,0] : [0,1];
      // HSH^T scalar
      const HSHt = H[0]*(state.Sigma[0][0]*H[0]+state.Sigma[0][1]*H[1])
                 + H[1]*(state.Sigma[1][0]*H[0]+state.Sigma[1][1]*H[1]);
      const den = HSHt + r;
      // K = Sigma H^T / (HSH^T + r)  in 2D it's a 2-vector
      const K = [(state.Sigma[0][0]*H[0]+state.Sigma[0][1]*H[1])/den,
                 (state.Sigma[1][0]*H[0]+state.Sigma[1][1]*H[1])/den];
      // Sigma <- (I - K H) Sigma
      const KH = [[K[0]*H[0], K[0]*H[1]],[K[1]*H[0], K[1]*H[1]]];
      const I = [[1,0],[0,1]];
      const ImKH = [[I[0][0]-KH[0][0], I[0][1]-KH[0][1]],
                    [I[1][0]-KH[1][0], I[1][1]-KH[1][1]]];
      state.Sigma = matmul(ImKH, state.Sigma);
      // keep symmetric
      state.Sigma = [[state.Sigma[0][0], (state.Sigma[0][1]+state.Sigma[1][0])/2],
                     [(state.Sigma[0][1]+state.Sigma[1][0])/2, state.Sigma[1][1]]];
      state.phase = 'predict';
    }
    while(state.history.length > 3) state.history.shift();
    draw();
  }
  function ellipsePath(S, scale){
    const e = eig2(S);
    const a = scale*Math.sqrt(e.l1), b = scale*Math.sqrt(e.l2);
    const theta = Math.atan2(e.v1[1], e.v1[0])*180/Math.PI;
    // approximate with 64 points
    let d='';
    for(let i=0;i<=64;i++){
      const ph = 2*Math.PI*i/64;
      const x = a*Math.cos(ph), y = b*Math.sin(ph);
      const c = Math.cos(theta*Math.PI/180), s = Math.sin(theta*Math.PI/180);
      const X = x*c - y*s, Y = x*s + y*c;
      d += (i?'L':'M')+X.toFixed(2)+' '+Y.toFixed(2);
    }
    return d+'Z';
  }
  function draw(){
    while(svg.firstChild) svg.removeChild(svg.firstChild);
    // axes
    svg.appendChild(SVG('line',{x1:-160,y1:0,x2:160,y2:0,stroke:'var(--line)'}));
    svg.appendChild(SVG('line',{x1:0,y1:-160,x2:0,y2:160,stroke:'var(--line)'}));
    const tx = SVG('text',{x:160,y:-6,'font-size':10,fill:'var(--mute)','text-anchor':'end'}); tx.textContent='x'; svg.appendChild(tx);
    const ty = SVG('text',{x:6,y:-152,'font-size':10,fill:'var(--mute)'}); ty.textContent='y'; svg.appendChild(ty);
    const scale = 110;
    // ghost of last two
    const cols = ['var(--violet)','var(--blue)','var(--yellow)'];
    const labels = state.history.slice(-2).map(h=>h.label).concat([state.phase==='predict'?'current (about to predict)':'after predict']);
    state.history.slice(-2).forEach((h,i)=>{
      svg.appendChild(SVG('path',{d:ellipsePath(h.S, scale), fill:'none', stroke:cols[i],'stroke-width':1.2,'stroke-opacity':0.6,'stroke-dasharray':'4 3'}));
    });
    svg.appendChild(SVG('path',{d:ellipsePath(state.Sigma, scale), fill:'var(--yellow)','fill-opacity':0.1, stroke:'var(--yellow)','stroke-width':2}));
    // mark observed axis
    if(state.phase==='update'){
      const axisCol = 'var(--pink)';
      if(state.mode==='x'){
        svg.appendChild(SVG('line',{x1:-150,y1:0,x2:150,y2:0,stroke:axisCol,'stroke-width':1.5,'stroke-dasharray':'5 3','stroke-opacity':0.7}));
      } else {
        svg.appendChild(SVG('line',{x1:0,y1:-150,x2:0,y2:150,stroke:axisCol,'stroke-width':1.5,'stroke-dasharray':'5 3','stroke-opacity':0.7}));
      }
    }
    const e = eig2(state.Sigma);
    out.textContent = 'next: '+state.phase+'    obs: '+state.mode+'-axis    Σ eigenvalues = '+
      e.l1.toFixed(3)+', '+e.l2.toFixed(3)+'    det Σ = '+(e.l1*e.l2).toFixed(4);
  }
  function setMode(m){
    state.mode = m;
    modeX.classList.toggle('active', m==='x');
    modeY.classList.toggle('active', m==='y');
    draw();
  }
  modeX.addEventListener('click', ()=> setMode('x'));
  modeY.addEventListener('click', ()=> setMode('y'));
  stepBtn.addEventListener('click', step);
  resetBtn.addEventListener('click', reset);
  reset();
})();
</script>

Pick the $y$-axis to observe and the predict step's shear has more to fix; pick the $x$-axis and the cross-correlation is what gets collapsed.

5. The Kalman gain as optimal mixing

The matrix $K_t = \Sigma_{t\mid t-1}H^\top(H\Sigma_{t\mid t-1}H^\top + R)^{-1}$ is forced on you by an optimality principle. Hold the prior $\Sigma_{t\mid t-1}$ fixed and ask: among all linear update rules $\hat x_{t\mid t} = \hat x_{t\mid t-1} + L\,(y_t - H\hat x_{t\mid t-1})$ (the residual in parentheses is called the innovation), which $L$ minimises the trace of the posterior covariance? Differentiating in $L$ and setting the gradient to zero gives $L = K_t$ on the nose. Three estimation frameworks land at the same matrix:

  • MMSE (minimum mean-squared error) — pick $\hat x$ to minimise $\mathbb{E}\|\hat x - x\|^2$ given $y$.
  • MAP (maximum a posteriori) — pick the $\hat x$ that maximises $p(x\mid y)$; equivalently, minimises $\tfrac12(x-\hat x_{t\mid t-1})^\top\Sigma^{-1}(\cdots) + \tfrac12(y-Hx)^\top R^{-1}(\cdots)$.
  • WLS (weighted least squares) — stack the prediction $\hat x_{t\mid t-1}$ and the $m$-dimensional observation $y_t$ as a joint residual and minimise with the inverse-noise weight matrices.

This three-way agreement is special to the linear-Gaussian world — once the model is nonlinear or the noise is heavy-tailed, the three frameworks disagree and Kalman becomes a heuristic instead of an exact filter.

A concrete check: with prior $\Sigma_{\mathrm{pred}}=\begin{pmatrix}1 & 0\\ 0 & 0.5\end{pmatrix}$, $H=[1\;0]$, $R=0.25$, the innovation covariance is $H\Sigma H^\top + R = 1.25$ and $K = \Sigma H^\top/1.25 = (0.8,\,0)^\top$. The filter moves $\hat x$ by $0.8$ of the residual in the $x$-direction; the unobserved $y$-coordinate is unmoved because the prior was uncorrelated. After update, $\Sigma_{\mathrm{post}} = \mathrm{diag}(0.2,\,0.5)$ — the observed axis shrinks by the factor $R/(H\Sigma H^\top+R) = 0.2$; the unobserved axis is untouched.

The letter $R$ is overloaded across the section: here it is the observation-noise covariance; in LQR it is the control-effort cost matrix; in mathematical finance it can be the risk-free rate. They are conceptually different objects that happen to share the symbol — when reading LQG literature (the LQR + Kalman bundle) both $R$'s appear in the same equations, so context-switching is mandatory.

(function(){
  const svg = document.getElementById('gain-svg');
  const out = document.getElementById('gain-out');
  const Rs = document.getElementById('gain-R');
  const Rv = document.getElementById('gain-Rv');
  // Fixed prior covariance (visible asymmetric ellipse)
  const Sigma = [[0.9, 0.4],[0.4, 0.6]];
  // Observe x-coordinate: H = [1, 0]
  function eig2(A){
    const a=A[0][0], b=A[0][1], d=A[1][1];
    const tr = a+d, det = a*d - b*b;
    const disc = Math.max(0, tr*tr/4 - det);
    const l1 = tr/2 + Math.sqrt(disc), l2 = tr/2 - Math.sqrt(disc);
    let v1;
    if(Math.abs(b) > 1e-9) v1 = [b, l1-a];
    else v1 = (a >= d) ? [1,0] : [0,1];
    const n = Math.hypot(v1[0],v1[1])||1; v1=[v1[0]/n, v1[1]/n];
    return {l1:Math.max(1e-9,l1), l2:Math.max(1e-9,l2), v1};
  }
  function ellipsePath(S, scale){
    const e = eig2(S);
    const a = scale*Math.sqrt(e.l1), b = scale*Math.sqrt(e.l2);
    const theta = Math.atan2(e.v1[1], e.v1[0]);
    let d='';
    for(let i=0;i<=64;i++){
      const ph = 2*Math.PI*i/64;
      const x = a*Math.cos(ph), y = b*Math.sin(ph);
      const c = Math.cos(theta), s = Math.sin(theta);
      const X = x*c - y*s, Y = x*s + y*c;
      d += (i?'L':'M')+X.toFixed(2)+' '+Y.toFixed(2);
    }
    return d+'Z';
  }
  function draw(){
    while(svg.firstChild) svg.removeChild(svg.firstChild);
    svg.appendChild(SVG('line',{x1:-160,y1:0,x2:160,y2:0,stroke:'var(--line)'}));
    svg.appendChild(SVG('line',{x1:0,y1:-160,x2:0,y2:160,stroke:'var(--line)'}));
    const R = parseFloat(Rs.value);
    Rv.textContent = 'R = '+R.toFixed(2);
    // K = Sigma H^T / (H Sigma H^T + R), with H=[1,0]
    const HSHt = Sigma[0][0];
    const K = [Sigma[0][0]/(HSHt+R), Sigma[1][0]/(HSHt+R)];
    // posterior Sigma = (I - K H) Sigma; with H=[1,0] this is
    // Sigma' = Sigma - K * [Sigma[0][0], Sigma[0][1]]
    const Sp = [
      [Sigma[0][0] - K[0]*Sigma[0][0], Sigma[0][1] - K[0]*Sigma[0][1]],
      [Sigma[1][0] - K[1]*Sigma[0][0], Sigma[1][1] - K[1]*Sigma[0][1]]
    ];
    // symmetrise for display
    Sp[0][1] = Sp[1][0] = (Sp[0][1]+Sp[1][0])/2;
    const scale = 110;
    // prior

    // posterior
    svg.appendChild(SVG('path',{d:ellipsePath(Sp, scale), fill:'var(--yellow)','fill-opacity':0.15, stroke:'var(--yellow)','stroke-width':2}));
    // x-axis observation indicator
    svg.appendChild(SVG('line',{x1:-150,y1:0,x2:150,y2:0,stroke:'var(--pink)','stroke-width':1.5,'stroke-opacity':0.6,'stroke-dasharray':'5 3'}));
    // legend
    const lg = SVG('g',{transform:'translate(-170,-170)'});
    [['var(--blue)','prior','dash'], ['var(--yellow)','posterior','solid'], ['var(--pink)','observed axis','dash']].forEach(([c,n,k],i)=>{
      lg.appendChild(SVG('line',{x1:0,y1:8+i*14,x2:18,y2:8+i*14,stroke:c,'stroke-width':2,'stroke-dasharray': k==='dash'?'4 3':null}));
      const t = SVG('text',{x:24,y:12+i*14,'font-size':11,fill:'var(--mute)'}); t.textContent=n; lg.appendChild(t);
    });
    svg.appendChild(lg);
    const ep = eig2(Sp), e = eig2(Sigma);
    out.textContent = 'K = ['+K[0].toFixed(3)+', '+K[1].toFixed(3)+']    '+
      'prior det = '+(e.l1*e.l2).toFixed(4)+'    post det = '+(ep.l1*ep.l2).toFixed(4)+
      '    shrink ratio = '+((ep.l1*ep.l2)/(e.l1*e.l2)).toFixed(3);
  }
  Rs.addEventListener('input', draw); draw();
})();
</script>

6. Tracking a 2D moving target

Lift to the running example that built the whole field. The constant-velocity (CV) model treats acceleration as white noise: state is $(p_x,p_y,v_x,v_y)$, dynamics over time-step $\Delta t$ propagate position by $v\Delta t$ and leave velocity nominally unchanged, with all uncertainty injected through the acceleration channel.

$$F = \begin{pmatrix}1 & 0 & \Delta t & 0\\ 0 & 1 & 0 & \Delta t\\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 0\\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 1\end{pmatrix},\qquad H = \begin{pmatrix}1 & 0 & 0 & 0\\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 0\end{pmatrix}.$$

The sensor sees only position, never velocity directly. Yet $\Sigma_t$ develops nonzero $(p,v)$ off-diagonal entries after a few steps — exactly because the filter has noticed that the residuals $y_t - H\hat x_{t\mid t-1}$ are correlated across time in a way consistent with a moving target.

Watch the off-diagonal coupling appear in one step. Take the 1D slice $(p,v)$ with $F=\begin{pmatrix}1 & \Delta t\\ 0 & 1\end{pmatrix}$ and a diagonal prior $\Sigma_0 = \mathrm{diag}(\sigma_p^2,\sigma_v^2)$. Then

$$F\Sigma_0 F^\top = \begin{pmatrix}\sigma_p^2 + \Delta t^2\sigma_v^2 & \Delta t\,\sigma_v^2\\ \Delta t\,\sigma_v^2 & \sigma_v^2\end{pmatrix}.$$

The off-diagonal $\Delta t\,\sigma_v^2$ wasn't there a moment ago. Add the CV process noise $Q$ (which also has a $\Delta t^2/2$ off-diagonal — see the quiz) and the coupling deepens. Once the prior has that off-diagonal, the next position observation's update touches the velocity components too: that's mechanically how observing only positions improves the velocity estimate. Eliminating velocity from the picture by hand throws this signal away; that's the whole reason the Kalman tracker beats every naive position-only smoother.

    const t = i*dt;
    return {px: 1.4*Math.sin(0.8*t), py: 0.9*Math.sin(1.3*t + 0.7)};
  });
  // deterministic noise streams
  function makeStream(seed){
    let s = seed >>> 0;
    return () => {
      s = (s*1664525+1013904223)>>>0;
      const u1 = s/4294967296;
      s = (s*1664525+1013904223)>>>0;
      const u2 = s/4294967296;
      return Math.sqrt(-2*Math.log(u1+1e-9))*Math.cos(2*Math.PI*u2);
    };
  }
  let state, raf=null;
  function reset(){
    state = {
      t: 0,
      x: [0,0,0,0],
      P: [[0.5,0,0,0],[0,0.5,0,0],[0,0,0.3,0],[0,0,0,0.3]],
      filtered: [],
      ells: [],
      obs: [],
      stream: makeStream(31337),
      playing: false
    };
    playBtn.textContent = 'play';
    draw();
  }
  // 4x4 helpers (specialised)
  function predict(x, P, q){
    // F is constant; F x:
    const xn = [x[0]+dt*x[2], x[1]+dt*x[3], x[2], x[3]];
    // P' = F P F^T + Q
    // F P:
    const FP = [
      [P[0][0]+dt*P[2][0], P[0][1]+dt*P[2][1], P[0][2]+dt*P[2][2], P[0][3]+dt*P[2][3]],
      [P[1][0]+dt*P[3][0], P[1][1]+dt*P[3][1], P[1][2]+dt*P[3][2], P[1][3]+dt*P[3][3]],
      [P[2][0], P[2][1], P[2][2], P[2][3]],
      [P[3][0], P[3][1], P[3][2], P[3][3]]
    ];
    // (F P) F^T:
    const FPFt = [
      [FP[0][0]+dt*FP[0][2], FP[0][1]+dt*FP[0][3], FP[0][2], FP[0][3]],
      [FP[1][0]+dt*FP[1][2], FP[1][1]+dt*FP[1][3], FP[1][2], FP[1][3]],
      [FP[2][0]+dt*FP[2][2], FP[2][1]+dt*FP[2][3], FP[2][2], FP[2][3]],
      [FP[3][0]+dt*FP[3][2], FP[3][1]+dt*FP[3][3], FP[3][2], FP[3][3]]
    ];
    // Q: pump noise into the velocity components (classic CV-model Q)
    const Qm = [
      [q*dt*dt*dt/3, 0, q*dt*dt/2, 0],
      [0, q*dt*dt*dt/3, 0, q*dt*dt/2],
      [q*dt*dt/2, 0, q*dt, 0],
      [0, q*dt*dt/2, 0, q*dt]
    ];
    const Pn = FPFt.map((row,i)=> row.map((v,j)=> v + Qm[i][j]));
    return {x:xn, P:Pn};
  }
  function update(x, P, y, r){
    // H = [[1,0,0,0],[1,0]:[0,1,0,0]]
    // innovation S = H P H^T + R = top-left 2x2 of P plus r I
    const S = [[P[0][0]+r, P[0][1]],[P[1][0], P[1][1]+r]];
    const detS = S[0][0]*S[1][1] - S[0][1]*S[1][0];
    const Sinv = [[S[1][1]/detS, -S[0][1]/detS],[-S[1][0]/detS, S[0][0]/detS]];
    // K = P H^T S^-1, shape 4x2
    const PHt = [[P[0][0], P[0][1]],[P[1][0], P[1][1]],[P[2][0], P[2][1]],[P[3][0], P[3][1]]];
    const K = PHt.map(row => [
      row[0]*Sinv[0][0]+row[1]*Sinv[1][0],
      row[0]*Sinv[0][1]+row[1]*Sinv[1][1]
    ]);
    // y - H x
    const innov = [y[0]-x[0], y[1]-x[1]];
    const xn = x.map((v,i)=> v + K[i][0]*innov[0] + K[i][1]*innov[1]);
    // P' = (I - K H) P
    // K H is 4x4 with first two columns = K[*][0], K[*][1] and last two = 0
    const KH = [
      [K[0][0], K[0][1], 0, 0],
      [K[1][0], K[1][1], 0, 0],
      [K[2][0], K[2][1], 0, 0],
      [K[3][0], K[3][1], 0, 0]
    ];
    const ImKH = [
      [1-KH[0][0], -KH[0][1], 0, 0],
      [-KH[1][0], 1-KH[1][1], 0, 0],
      [-KH[2][0], -KH[2][1], 1, 0],
      [-KH[3][0], -KH[3][1], 0, 1]
    ];
    const Pn = [0,1,2,3].map(i=> [0,1,2,3].map(j=>
      ImKH[i][0]*P[0][j]+ImKH[i][1]*P[1][j]+ImKH[i][2]*P[2][j]+ImKH[i][3]*P[3][j]));
    return {x:xn, P:Pn};
  }
  function eig2(A00,A01,A11){
    const tr = A00+A11, det = A00*A11 - A01*A01;
    const disc = Math.max(0, tr*tr/4 - det);
    const l1 = tr/2 + Math.sqrt(disc), l2 = tr/2 - Math.sqrt(disc);
    let v1;
    if(Math.abs(A01) > 1e-9) v1 = [A01, l1-A00];
    else v1 = (A00 >= A11) ? [1,0] : [0,1];
    const n = Math.hypot(v1[0],v1[1])||1; v1=[v1[0]/n, v1[1]/n];
    return {l1:Math.max(1e-12,l1), l2:Math.max(1e-12,l2), v1};
  }
  function tick(){
    if(state.t >= N){ pause(); return; }
    const q = parseFloat(qSl.value);
    const r = parseFloat(rSl.value);
    let {x, P} = predict(state.x, state.P, q);
    const tr = truth[state.t];
    const y = [tr.px + Math.sqrt(r)*state.stream(), tr.py + Math.sqrt(r)*state.stream()];
    ({x, P} = update(x, P, y, r));
    state.x = x; state.P = P;
    state.filtered.push({px:x[0], py:x[1]});
    state.obs.push({x:y[0], y:y[1]});
    state.ells.push({P00:P[0][0], P01:P[0][1], P11:P[1][1], px:x[0], py:x[1]});
    state.t += 1;
    draw();
    if(state.playing) raf = requestAnimationFrame(tick);
  }
  function play(){
    if(state.playing){ pause(); return; }
    if(state.t >= N) reset();
    state.playing = true; playBtn.textContent = 'pause';
    raf = requestAnimationFrame(tick);
  }
  function pause(){ state.playing = false; playBtn.textContent='play'; if(raf) cancelAnimationFrame(raf); }
  function draw(){
    while(svg.firstChild) svg.removeChild(svg.firstChild);
    const X = px => 100*px;
    const Y = py => -100*py;
    // axes
    svg.appendChild(SVG('line',{x1:-180,y1:0,x2:180,y2:0,stroke:'var(--line)','stroke-dasharray':'3 3'}));
    svg.appendChild(SVG('line',{x1:0,y1:-110,x2:0,y2:110,stroke:'var(--line)','stroke-dasharray':'3 3'}));
    // truth curve (ground truth in full)
    let dT='';
    for(let i=0;i<N;i++) dT += (i?'L':'M')+X(truth[i].px).toFixed(2)+' '+Y(truth[i].py).toFixed(2);
    svg.appendChild(SVG('path',{d:dT,fill:'none',stroke:'var(--cyan)','stroke-width':1.4,'stroke-opacity':0.45}));
    // observations
    state.obs.forEach(o=>{
      svg.appendChild(SVG('circle',{cx:X(o.x),cy:Y(o.y),r:1.4,fill:'var(--pink)','fill-opacity':0.7}));
    });
    // filtered curve
    if(state.filtered.length){
      let dF='';
      state.filtered.forEach((p,i)=> dF += (i?'L':'M')+X(p.px).toFixed(2)+' '+Y(p.py).toFixed(2));
      svg.appendChild(SVG('path',{d:dF,fill:'none',stroke:'var(--yellow)','stroke-width':2}));
    }
    // sparse ellipses (every ~8th step) showing position-block of covariance
    state.ells.forEach((e,i)=>{
      if(i%8 !== 0 && i !== state.ells.length-1) return;
      const eig = eig2(e.P00, e.P01, e.P11);
      const a = 100*1.5*Math.sqrt(eig.l1), b = 100*1.5*Math.sqrt(eig.l2);
      const theta = Math.atan2(eig.v1[1], eig.v1[0])*180/Math.PI;
      const g = SVG('g',{transform:`translate(${X(e.px).toFixed(2)} ${Y(e.py).toFixed(2)}) rotate(${(-theta).toFixed(2)})`});
      g.appendChild(SVG('ellipse',{cx:0,cy:0,rx:a.toFixed(2),ry:b.toFixed(2),fill:'none',stroke:'var(--yellow)','stroke-opacity':0.45,'stroke-width':1}));
      svg.appendChild(g);
    });
    // legend
    const lg = SVG('g',{transform:'translate(-195,-120)'});
    [['var(--cyan)','truth',true], ['var(--yellow)','filter',true], ['var(--pink)','obs',false]].forEach(([c,n2,line],i)=>{
      if(line){ lg.appendChild(SVG('line',{x1:0,y1:6+i*12,x2:14,y2:6+i*12,stroke:c,'stroke-width':2})); }
      else { lg.appendChild(SVG('circle',{cx:7,cy:6+i*12,r:2,fill:c})); }
      const t = SVG('text',{x:18,y:9+i*12,'font-size':10,fill:'var(--mute)'}); t.textContent=n2; lg.appendChild(t);
    });
    svg.appendChild(lg);
    const last = state.ells.length ? state.ells[state.ells.length-1] : null;
    if(last){
      const sd = Math.sqrt((last.P00+last.P11)/2);
      out.textContent = 't='+state.t+'/'+N+'    position 1σ ≈ '+sd.toFixed(3)+
        '    velocity uncertainty via off-diagonal: '+state.P[0][2].toFixed(3);
    } else {
      out.textContent = 'press play to start';
    }
  }
  playBtn.addEventListener('click', play);
  resetBtn.addEventListener('click', ()=>{ pause(); reset(); });
  [qSl, rSl].forEach(el=> el.addEventListener('input', ()=>{
    if(!state.playing) draw();
    else { /* parameters take effect on next tick */ }
  }));
  reset();
})();
</script>

Two qualitative behaviours to play with:

  • Crank $R$ up — sensor goes noisy. The filter trusts its dynamic model more and the yellow trace becomes a smoothed version of the truth that lags the high-frequency wiggles in the observations.
  • Crank $Q$ up — process noise admits the model could be wrong. The filter trusts observations more and chases each measurement; uncertainty ellipses stay roughly the same size but the trace gets jittery.
The diagonal of $Q$ in this widget is structured as $q\cdot\bigl(\Delta t^3/3,\Delta t^3/3,\Delta t,\Delta t\bigr)$ with off-diagonal $q\Delta t^2/2$ couplings — the standard "noise on acceleration, propagated through the kinematics" choice for a CV model. That structure is why the velocity components stay correlated with positions through prediction.

Connections

Kalman is exact only in the linear-Gaussian box. The frontier is everything outside it — nonlinear dynamics (EKF, UKF), non-Gaussian posteriors (particle filters), partial observability with unknown parameters (joint state-parameter estimation), and the data-association problem (which measurement corresponds to which target). Variational and message-passing formulations recover Kalman as a special case of belief propagation on a Gaussian factor graph, opening the door to large-scale graphical-model inference.

  • Optimal control — Linear-quadratic regulator — LQR pairs with the Kalman filter to give LQG, the canonical separation-principle controller for noisy linear systems.
  • Stochastic calculus — applications — the continuous-time Kalman–Bucy filter is a Riccati ODE driven by an innovation process; the discrete recursion is its sampled version.
  • Mathematical finance — Itô diffusions — latent-volatility models for option pricing reduce to a Kalman update when the volatility-driving SDE is linearised around the current estimate.
  • Probability theory — conditional probability and Bayes — the entire filter is one repeated Bayesian update, made tractable by closure of the Gaussian family.
  • Convex optimization — gradient methods — the WLS view of the update recasts Kalman as a recursive quadratic optimisation step, the natural bridge to recursive estimation in machine learning.
